A Palestinian-American has returned to his village of Qusra to protect it from increasing settler attacks, which have surged amid ongoing settlement expansion. stories.summary: A charter plane carrying eight people crashed near a U.S. military-managed radar site in western Alaska, resulting in the deaths of all on board. The plane, a Cessna 441, reportedly went down on approach to Cape Newenham. An investigation into the incident is currently underway.

stories.title: Ebola Outbreak in DRC Surges as Death Toll Exceeds 2,500
stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is escalating rapidly, with the United Nations reporting that the death toll has surpassed 2,500. This outbreak is now the most severe in the country's recent history and is spreading at a significant rate, affecting an area larger than France. The World Health Organization is responding by supplying thousands of vaccine doses to help contain the virus.

stories.title: Israel Advances E1 West Bank Settlement Amid International Backlash
stories.summary: Israel has re-established the E1 settlement in the West Bank, allowing thirty families to move in, which has sparked fears among nearby Palestinian residents. The project has drawn significant international condemnation, particularly from France, Germany, the UK, and Italy, who argue that it undermines the possibility of a Palestinian state by further partitioning the occupied territory. The settlement plan, which includes over 1,200 homes, has been criticized as a violation of international law.

stories.title: Aisha Wahab Wins Special Election for California's 14th Congressional District
stories.summary: Aisha Wahab has won the special election to fill the remainder of Eric Swalwell's term in California's 14th Congressional District. Wahab, a state senator, defeated fellow Democrat Melissa Hernandez. This victory makes her the first Afghan American elected to Congress. The partial term will conclude in January 2027, after which a new candidate will be elected for the full term in November.

stories.title: DR Congo to Receive 70,000 Doses of Ervebo Vaccine Amid Ebola Outbreak
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is set to receive 70,000 doses of the Ervebo vaccine to combat a surge in Ebola infections, particularly the Bundibugyo strain. The World Health Organization (WHO) has indicated that while it is uncertain if Ervebo will protect against this specific strain, preliminary laboratory and animal studies suggest it may offer some level of protection. A new trial will aim to determine the vaccine's efficacy in humans.

stories.title: Personalized mRNA Cancer Treatment Shows Promise Against Melanoma in Trial
stories.summary: Merck and Moderna announced that their personalized mRNA cancer treatment has successfully reduced melanoma tumor recurrence in a late-stage clinical trial. This marks a significant milestone in cancer treatment, as it is the first time an mRNA-based drug has shown positive results in such a large trial. Researchers are optimistic about the potential for this approach to be applied to other types of cancer in the future.
